title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Page 25 opens with 'On reprend tout !', so Grothendieck abandons the approach of pp. 20-24 (the 'multilistes' X in M, compared by refinement and compatibility). There he had found that M could be recovered from a ground set L together with families L̂_X in P(P(L)). He now turns that observation into the primitive definition.

**Définition-scholie.** A 'contrée' C consists of:
- a set L, the 'lieux' (places) of the contrée;
- a set 𝓕 ⊂ P(P(L)) whose elements are called 'figures', so that 𝓕 ∈ P(P(P(L))).

An element X of a figure F is a subset of L, called a (closed) 'strate' of F. The union of the closed strata of F is the 'support' |F| ⊂ L. The axioms 'Cont n' are to be extracted as the work proceeds ('qui vont être dégagés par la suite').

**Cont 1.**
- (a) The empty subset of P(L) is a figure, the 'figure vide'. It is the unique figure without strata, with empty support.
- (b) For every place x ∈ L there is a figure whose unique stratum is {x}, the 'figure ponctuelle' {{x}}.

**Context from p. 26.** Cont 2 says that for each X ∈ F the open stratum X° = X \ ∂X is nonempty, where ∂X is the union of the strata of F strictly below X ('admissibilité'). It also says that the intersection of two closed strata is a union of closed strata, i.e. the frontier condition. The X° then partition |F|, and a figure becomes an abstract 'stratified partition' of a subset of L, presented by its poset of closed strata.

**Modern reading.** This is an axiomatic, point-set-free (no topology on L assumed) framework for tame topology: a 'space' is a set of places with a distinguished class of admissible (presumably finite) closed stratifications. Topology and geometry are meant to be recovered from the figures, in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' programme of Esquisse d'un programme §5-6. A figure's poset of strata is a finite poset, i.e. a finite T0 (Alexandrov) space, so each figure carries a combinatorial shape. The closest modern frameworks are o-minimal structures (definable sets as primitives) and stratified spaces with frontier condition / exit-path categories. On this page only the definitions and the trivial axiom Cont 1 are stated.
errors: No mathematical error. Cont 1(a) is tautologically consistent: the empty family of subsets is the unique figure with no strata. Finiteness of figures, presumably intended, is not yet imposed on this page.

The machine transcription's 'Le nombre des strates ... est appelé le support' misreads the manuscript, which says 'La réunion des strates ...'. Read as 'number', the definition of |F| would be wrong and inconsistent with p. 26, which uses |F| as a subset of L.

ideas.what: Contrée: a set L of 'lieux' with a family of 'figures' (sets of closed strata, subsets of L); topology is not given but encoded by the admissible stratifications
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology via admissible stratifications; compare o-minimal structures, 'tame' stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Knight-Pillay-Steinhorn (1980s), van den Dries 1998 book; Grothendieck's tame topology programme: Esquisse d'un programme (1984)
ideas.where_published: Programmatic idea in Esquisse d'un programme §5-6; this specific axiomatization (contrée/lieux/figures/strates) appears unpublished

ideas.modern_name: stratification with frontier condition; poset of strata / finite T0 space
ideas.where_published: Stratifications discussed in Esquisse d'un programme; no formal axioms published

missed.claim: Grothendieck starts a set-theoretic axiomatization of 'tame' spaces ('contrées') in which the primitive data are the admissible stratifications ('figures') rather than open sets or definable sets. The axioms are explicitly left to be 'dégagés par la suite'. This is a concrete, unpublished starting point for the tame topology he called for in the Esquisse, and differs from o-minimality in taking stratifications themselves as primitive.
missed.quote: Une contrée est définie par un ensemble L (l'ens. des lieux de la contrée), et la donnée de certains ensembles de parties de L, appelées les figures ... On pose des axiomes des contrées, qui vont être dégagés par la suite.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Current work on tame geometry (o-minimal, tame stratified spaces, exit-path ∞-categories, 'tame topology' via condensed / definable methods) lacks a stratification-first foundation. Grothendieck's contrée axioms could be compared with these frameworks, especially if later pages complete the axiom list.

deep.surprise_reason: A foundational definition page of Grothendieck's unpublished 'Analysis situs' tame topology project with new terminology (contrée, lieux, figures, strates, support). The concept is of historical interest and essentially unknown in the literature, but this page contains only definitions and a trivial axiom.
transcription_corrections: 'Le nombre des strates' should read 'La réunion des strates' (support = union of strata).
'([-formes-])' after 'strates' is most likely '(fermées)', i.e. closed strata, consistent with p. 26; likewise the struck word in 'des strates [-formes-] de F' is likely 'fermées'.
'L'ens. 𝓕 des figures de C est donc [-un ensemble-] partie de P(P(L))': the struck text is 'un ensemble' and the word 'une' should precede 'partie'.
Cont 1(a): 'C'est donc la figure unique qui n'a pas de strates' is correct.
Cont 1(b): 'il y a une figure ayant pour strates unique {x}'; the word 'pour' is missing in the transcription.
The left-margin note near Cont 1 is barely legible; possibly 'ce qui donne les lieux' or similar, so the transcription's guess is uncertain.
